newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Detained Israelis in Cyprus claim brutality.
newsitem.headline: Detained Israelis in Cyprus claim brutality.

text.p: A Cypriot court ordered a police probe on Tuesday into allegations four Israeli prisoners were beaten by prison guards when one of them complained about the food he was served.

Nicosia district judge Charis Malaktos ordered the probe after Avi Biton, 21, his brother David, 24, Shuki Samana, 24, and Amon Shimon, 28, appeared at the courthouse shouting that they had been beaten.

"I asked for food and they hit me," David Biton told reporters as he was pulled into the courtroom, naked from the waist up and handcuffed to a policeman. He displayed a bandaged left arm and swore at police.
All four have been charged in connection with an escape bid earlier this month.

Police charged Avi Biton and Samana with escaping detention while being taken to court for another case on September 11. David Biton and Shimon were charged with assisting their escape, possession of firearms, conspiring to commit a crime and causing damage to a police vehicle.
The court ordered a trial for October 30. None answered the charges, and they will remain in custody until then.

Cyprus prisons director George Anastassiades told Reuters he would investigate the complaint as directed by the court but said "from verbal evidence I have recieved so far it appears these claims are not true."
Police say Avi Biton and Shuki Samana fled into the Turkish-held north of Cyprus after David Biton and Shimon waylaid a police car taking them to court. Turkish Cypriot police returned them.
